steps: A client, first call to placement
After the call, and the CRM

check1.q: An owner keeps bringing up price on a first call. What is usually underneath it?
o: Price really is the barrier, so lead with what they save
Whether they can trust the person, and whether the person becomes another job
Where the professional lives
The time zone
check1.w: Owners rarely hesitate over price or geography. The two real fears are trust and burden, and everything we say answers one of them.

check1.q: Which of these businesses is the strongest fit for Relève?
o: A 200-person company with its own HR team
A London agency with six staff
A US coach with four people, $45,000 a month in revenue, still answering their own inbox
A restaurant that needs someone at the front desk
check1.w: Our client is a US owner with one to ten people and at least $30,000 a month, still doing too much of the day-to-day. We don’t take on-site roles, clients outside the US, or larger companies.

check1.q: Which of these is one of the six fronts every professional is vetted on?
o: Both sides take the Relève Signature™, so the fit is designed
The lowest hourly rate in the market
A shortlist of five resumes for the owner
A start within 48 hours
check1.w: The six fronts: the business studied first, tested for the role, matched to how you work through the Signature, identity verified, one candidate presented, and approved by name.

check1.q: A prospect mentions another staffing company by name. How do you respond?
o: Point out the weaknesses in their reviews
Say they use cheaper talent
Change the subject
Agree with what is true about the option, then move to the cost the owner has already felt
check1.w: We never name or criticise another company. Agree with what’s true, then talk about the hours spent finding, starting and replacing a hire that didn’t work.

check1.q: What does an owner see when Relève presents a candidate?
o: A ranked shortlist
One candidate, with the Signature Match explaining why we chose them
The full roster to browse
The candidate’s pay, so they can compare
check1.w: One candidate at a time, with the Signature Match: the reasoning, where they line up, and what is worth knowing before the call. Clients never see talent pay.

o: $950 a month, full time
$950 a month for up to 15 hours a week, on a three-month term
$2,500 a month for up to 15 hours a week
$500 a month for up to 10 hours a week
check2.w: Starter is $950 a month, or $2,500 paid in full for each three-month term, with the professional’s hours capped at 15 a week.

o: Whenever the client changes their mind in the first week
At the end of the minimum term
Only if Relève never presents a candidate
If the client declines the first candidate
check2.w: The deposit is credited against the first invoice. It comes back in full only if Relève never presents anyone.

check2.q: A client on Essential wants to hire their professional directly. What applies?
o: A conversion fee of $30,000, twelve months of the plan
It isn’t allowed under any circumstances
Nothing, once six months have passed
A one-off fee of $2,500
check2.w: The conversion fee is twelve months of the plan: $11,400 on Starter, $30,000 on Essential and $54,000 on Specialist.

check2.q: A prospect asks for a two-month term at a lower price. What do you say?
o: Agree, to win the client
Offer the eLIVate discount instead
Decline and end the call
“Let me confirm that in writing for you,” then take it to Sage
check2.w: Never improvise a term. Anything not written in the terms is confirmed in writing after Sage has decided.

check2.q: What do eLIVate Club members receive?
o: 50% off their first month on any plan
$500 off each month for the first three months, on Essential and Specialist
$500 off Starter every month
A free month after six months
check2.w: Members get $500 off each month for the first three months on Essential and Specialist. It doesn’t apply to Starter.

check3.q: When does a client get an account in the app?
o: When they book a discovery call
When they open the free training
Only once Relève sends their onboarding email
When they fill in the form on the website
check3.w: Nobody enters the app without an onboarding email from Relève. Prospects and leads stay on the website.

check3.q: What must happen before an applicant can be invited onto the talent side?
o: A screening call that has actually taken place
Taking The Watch™
The Talent Signature
Their payout details
check3.w: We meet everyone. An application has to pass through a booked and held screening call before it can be invited.

check3.q: How do the Signature and the disciplines differ?
o: They measure the same thing twice
The disciplines are for clients only
The Signature is optional for talent
The Signature asks whether two people will work well together; the disciplines ask whether the person can do the job
check3.w: Neither answers the other’s question, which is why every match needs both.

check3.q: Who directs the professional’s day-to-day work?
o: The Talent Success Manager
The client
The console, automatically
The professional decides alone
check3.w: The client directs the daily work. Relève sets the scope and the recurring work of the role, runs the calls and reviews, and handles everything around it.

check3.q: When does Relève stop watching a placement?
o: At day 14
At day 90
Never while the placement lasts; day 90 only ends onboarding
After the six-month review
check3.w: The 90-Day Success Plan gets the professional up and running. We keep watching the work for as long as the client is with us.

check4.q: Which line is written in the Relève voice?
o: “Our seamless solution unlocks your growth.”
“Our VAs cost 70% less than a local hire.”
“Every professional is prepared for your role before day one.”
“Our trained VAs are managed for you.”
check4.w: We say “prepared for your role,” never “trained,” and we make no cost claims. Seamless and unlock are on the banned list.

check4.q: What is the first real question on a discovery call?
o: “What happened the last time you handed work to someone?”
“What’s your budget?”
“Have you looked at our pricing?”
“How many hours do you want back?”
check4.w: Everything on the call hangs off that answer. It tells you which fear to answer and which front to lean on.

check4.q: In the offer, what order do the plans come in?
o: Starter first, then the upsell
Only Essential
Let the owner choose from the website
Specialist and Essential first, then recommend Starter for their first column
check4.w: Heard after $4,500 and $2,500, Starter at $950 is an easy first step, and recommending the smaller plan builds trust.

check4.q: An owner says, “I need to think about it.” What do you do first?
o: Offer a discount
Acknowledge it, then find the one part they’re unsure about: the fit, the money or the timing
Send the pricing page
Agree, and follow up next month
check4.w: Acknowledge, isolate, answer, confirm. A maybe almost always hides one specific doubt.

check4.q: A call ends in a no. What happens next?
o: Nothing, out of respect
A follow-up call every day that week
Give them an app login so they can look around
Send the written audit anyway, then one short, low-pressure note two days later
check4.w: The audit is theirs to keep, and goodwill is where referrals and later yeses come from. Prospects never get a link into the app.

check5.q: A client asks what their professional is paid. What do you say?
o: Tell them, since they’re paying for it
Explain that pay is private on both sides, and that their retainer covers everything
Give them a rough range
Suggest they ask the professional
check5.w: Clients never see talent pay and talent never see the client’s rate. That wall is built into the app, and we keep it in every conversation.

check5.q: You’re emailing a prospect about Relève. Which account do you use?
o: hello@relevestaffing.com, writing as Relève
Your personal Gmail
Whichever is quickest
A LinkedIn message from your own profile, signed with your name
check5.w: Everything Relève runs through Relève accounts and goes out as Relève. The Relève Letter, written as Sage, is the only exception.

check5.q: A professional raises a concern about a client’s tone in their Friday report. What do you do?
o: Forward the report to the client
Wait to see whether it happens again
Read it, call the professional, and log what you did, keeping it private from the client
Mark it as resolved
check5.w: A concern needs a closer look the same day. What a professional tells their Talent Success Manager never goes to the client.

check5.q: Who is named as Relève’s founder in anything we write?
o: The whole team
Nobody
Whoever wrote the piece
Sage Jackson
check5.w: Sage Jackson is Relève’s founder. Never name anyone else.

check5.q: A client asks whether they can pause for a month without paying. You’re not sure. What do you say?
o: Yes, to keep them happy
No, never
“Let me confirm that in writing for you,” and ask Sage
Whatever seems fair at the time
check5.w: Never guess a term, a price or a promise. Confirm it in writing once it has been decided.
